question: Why can’t we predict if a program will halt on a given input?
answer: Suppose a program H can tell whether any program halts on its input. Add a twist: H+ takes its own code as input and does the opposite of whatever H predicts. Either way, H is wrong, so no program like H can exist.
move: No program can predict, for every program, whether it will halt.
